THE PLATFORM AT A GLANCE
Upload once. Search, analyze, or ask.
MARENGO · EMBED + SEARCH
Find it
Turns video, audio, images, and text into embeddings, so you can search footage in plain language.
PEGASUS · ANALYZE
Describe it
Watches a video and writes text: summaries, chapters, answers, JSON, or timed segments.
JOCKEY · AGENT
Ask it
An agent that plans its own steps across your whole library and answers with cited moments.
Models API: you choose exactly what runs. Agents API (Jockey): the agent picks the steps for you.

STEP 0  ·  PLAYGROUND
Test it in the Playground before you code
playground.twelvelabs.io
1  Upload videos and images in Assets
2  Run Search, Analyze, or Segment
3  Flip Visual to JSON for raw output
4  View Code copies the exact request

STEP 0  ·  API KEY
Get your API key and SDK in 2 minutes
1 Sign up
Free account at playground.twelvelabs.io
2 Create a key
Settings → API Keys → Create API Key. Copy it.
3 Install the SDK
Python or Node.js. Always install the latest version.
pip install --upgrade twelvelabs        # Python
npm install twelvelabs-js@latest        # Node.js
client = TwelveLabs(api_key=os.environ["TWELVELABS_API_KEY"])
Calling REST directly? Send the key in the x-api-key header to https://api.twelvelabs.io/v1.3

STEP 1  ·  ASSETS
Assets: upload once, reuse everywhere
Public URL  ·  up to 4 GB
Local file  ·  up to 200 MB
Multipart  ·  up to 10 GB
Then pass the asset_id to:
Indexes → Marengo search
Analyze → Pegasus text
Embed → Marengo vectors
Entities → player photos
Knowledge stores → Jockey
Processing is async: poll until status is "ready". Use direct media links. YouTube, Drive, and Dropbox links fail.

PART 1  ·  FIND IT
Marengo
Embeddings, indexes, search, and entity search

MARENGO  ·  EMBEDDING MODEL
Marengo turns video into searchable meaning
It watches the visuals, listens to speech and sound, and reads on-screen text. Each moment becomes an embedding (a vector), so similar moments sit close together.
Marengo 3.0: powers search inside an index
Marengo 3.5: embeddings you store yourself (128/256/512 dims)
Use it for semantic search, similar-play lookup, clustering, and RAG.
One plain-language query matches a character, an object, a logo, and an action.

MARENGO  ·  INDEX + SEARCH
Build an index, then search it
1  Create an index
2  Add your asset
3  Wait for "ready"
4  Search
index = client.indexes.create(
  index_name="spurs-games",
  models=[{"model_name": "marengo3.0",
           "model_options": ["visual", "audio"]}])

client.indexes.indexed_assets.create(
  index_id=index.id, asset_id=asset.id)

hits = client.search.query(index_id=index.id,
  query_text="corner three in transition",
  search_options=["visual", "audio"])
Each hit returns video_id, start, end (seconds), and rank (1 = best).

MARENGO  ·  ENTITY SEARCH (BETA)
Find a specific player with entities
1  Create a collection
One per roster, e.g. "Spurs"
2  Create an entity
A player + reference photos
3  Search with <@entity_id>
Mention the player in the query
roster = client.entity_collections.create(name="Spurs")

player = client.entity_collections.entities.create(
  entity_collection_id=roster.id,
  name="Player 1",
  asset_ids=[photo1.id, photo2.id, photo3.id])

hits = client.search.query(index_id=index.id,
  query_text=f"<@{player.id}> dunks on a fast break",
  search_options=["visual", "audio"])
Tips
Upload several clear photos per player: different angles, lighting, and jerseys
Keep each team in its own collection for better accuracy
Works on any index with Marengo enabled

PART 2  ·  DESCRIBE IT
Pegasus 1.6
General mode, structured JSON, and timed segments

PEGASUS  ·  VIDEO-LANGUAGE MODEL
Pegasus watches video and writes about it
Give it a video (or up to 20 images) and a prompt. It answers in text grounded in what it sees and hears.
General mode: prompt in, text or JSON out
Time-based metadata: timed segments out
Use pegasus1.6. Sync calls handle videos up to 1 hour; async tasks go longer.

PEGASUS  ·  GENERAL MODE
General mode: the parameters that matter
model_name

video

prompt

temperature

max_tokens

response_format

start_time / end_time

stream
Use "pegasus1.6". Omitting it falls back to pegasus1.5.

What to watch: an asset_id, a public URL, or base64.

Your instruction or question. Use prompt_v2 to reference images.

Randomness from 0 to 1. Default 0.2. Use 0 for repeatable output.

Cap on response length. Default 4,096 tokens.

Add a JSON schema to get structured output (next slide).

Analyze only part of the video, in seconds.

Sync only: stream text as it is generated. Default true.

PEGASUS  ·  STRUCTURED OUTPUT
Get JSON back with response_format
res = client.analyze(
  model_name="pegasus1.6",
  video=VideoContext_AssetId(asset_id=asset.id),
  prompt="List every basket and who scored.",
  response_format=SyncResponseFormat(
    type="json_schema",
    json_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {
      "plays": {"type": "array", "items": {
        "type": "object", "properties": {
          "player": {"type": "string"},
          "start_time": {"type": "number"}}}}}}))

data = json.loads(res.data)
The prompt says what to extract. The JSON schema sets the shape for the output.
res.data is a JSON string. Parse it before you use it.
finish_reason "stop" = complete. "length" = cut off: raise max_tokens.

PEGASUS  ·  TIME-BASED METADATA
Split a video into timed, tagged segments
Describe the segment types you want and the fields to fill. Pegasus returns each segment's start, end, and your fields.
Async only: create a task, then poll it
Set analysis_mode="time_based_metadata"
No prompt: your descriptions are the instructions
Up to 20 segment definitions per task
Tune length with min/max_segment_duration
Playground Segment: each block on the timeline is one segment with its own metadata.

PEGASUS  ·  TIME-BASED METADATA
Define segments, get timed JSON back
task = client.analyze_async.tasks.create(
  model_name="pegasus1.6",
  video=VideoContext_AssetId(asset_id=asset.id),
  analysis_mode="time_based_metadata",
  response_format=AsyncResponseFormat(
    type="segment_definitions",
    segment_definitions=[{
      "id": "possessions",
      "description": "Each offensive possession",
      "fields": [
        {"name": "result", "type": "string",
         "enum": ["score", "miss", "turnover"],
         "description": "How the possession ended"}]}]))

# poll analyze_async.tasks.retrieve(task.task_id)
What you get back
{"possessions": [
  {"start_time": 12.0,
   "end_time": 31.5,
   "metadata": {
     "result": "score"}},
  ...]}
Field types: string, number, integer, boolean, array, timestamp, time_array. Parse task.result.data when status is "ready".

PART 3  ·  ASK IT
Jockey
The video agent, knowledge stores, and the Agents API

JOCKEY  ·  VIDEO AGENT
Jockey: an agent that reasons over video
Ask in plain language. Jockey plans its own steps with Marengo and Pegasus and answers from every video in a knowledge store. DEMO
Answers grounded in the footage
Text or typed JSON (JSON Schema)
Follow-ups with session_id
instructions set the lens (scout, editor)
No code: connect.twelvelabs.io or MCP
Highlight reels  ·  Track a player across games  ·  Tag every play
Jockey inside Claude via MCP: mcp.twelvelabs.io/jockey/mcp

JOCKEY  ·  KNOWLEDGE STORE
A knowledge store is Jockey's memory
Your media, plus what Jockey learns:
Context: entities, moments, summaries
Ontology: a typed schema linking them
Embeddings: vectors for search
Items: queued → processing → ready. A query hits one store.
Upload and manage stores in Jockey Connect: connect.twelvelabs.io

JOCKEY  ·  AGENTS API
Fill a store, then ask it or search it
Setup:  knowledge_stores.create(name)  →  knowledge_store_items.create(store.id, asset_id)  →  poll until ready
Ask: a grounded answer (text or JSON)
resp = client.responses.create(
  knowledge_store_id=store.id,
  input=[{"type": "message",
          "role": "user",
          "content": "List every 3-pointer"}])

for o in resp.output:
  if o.type == "message":
    print(o.content[0].text)
Search: ranked clips with start and end
r = client.knowledge_stores.search(
  knowledge_store_id=store.id,
  query={"text": "crowd celebrates"},
  search_options={"video": {
    "modalities": ["visual", "audio"]}})

for hit in r.data:
  m = hit.matches[0]
  print(hit.rank, m.start_sec, m.end_sec)

CHEAT SHEET  ·  MODELS API
The Models API on one page
Python calls on client = TwelveLabs(api_key=...)  ·  REST base: https://api.twelvelabs.io/v1.3
Upload media  ·  POST /assets
assets.create(method="url", url=...)
Create an index  ·  POST /indexes
indexes.create(index_name, models=[...])
Index an asset  ·  POST /indexes/{id}/indexed-assets
indexes.indexed_assets.create(index_id, asset_id)
Search moments  ·  POST /search
search.query(index_id, query_text, search_options)
Create an entity  ·  POST /entity-collections
entity_collections.entities.create(id, name, asset_ids)
Embeddings (Marengo 3.5)  ·  POST /embed-v2
embed.v_2.create(model_name="marengo3.5", ...)
Text or JSON (Pegasus)  ·  POST /analyze
analyze(model_name="pegasus1.6", video, prompt)
Timed segments  ·  POST /analyze/tasks
analyze_async.tasks.create(analysis_mode=...)

CHEAT SHEET  ·  AGENTS API (JOCKEY)
The Agents API on one page
Same client, same assets. Upload once, then add the asset_id to a store.
Upload media  ·  POST /assets
assets.create(method="url", url=...)
Create a store  ·  POST /knowledge-stores
knowledge_stores.create(name=...)
Add an item  ·  POST /knowledge-stores/{id}/items
knowledge_store_items.create(..., asset_id=...)
Poll until ready  ·  GET .../items/{item_id}
knowledge_store_items.retrieve(...).status
Ask a question  ·  POST /responses
responses.create(knowledge_store_id, input=[...])
Search clips  ·  POST /knowledge-stores/{id}/search
knowledge_stores.search(..., query={"text": ...})
Extras on responses.create: session_id for follow-ups, instructions for a lens, text=TextParam(...) for JSON.

BEFORE YOU BUILD
Six things that save you an hour
Direct media links only
Use an .mp4 URL or a local file. No YouTube or Drive.
Everything is async
Poll assets, indexing, and store items until ready.
Use a fresh SDK
pip install --upgrade twelvelabs before you start.
Pick the right Marengo
Index search uses 3.0. Use 3.5 for embeddings.
Use Pegasus 1.6
Pass model_name="pegasus1.6" on every analyze call.
Retry the right errors
Retry 429 and 5xx with backoff. Fix other 4xx errors.
